Welcome to Scratchnapped! :)

I'm Griffpatch, and I'm so pleased you are here.  I wish that all these scripts were super easy to follow, but I'm afraid they are quite probably not :/.  I have tried my best to keep things as simple as possible and will at some point try to document everything... but until then feel free to play around with what you see and try to figure things out.  Let me give you a quick guide:
So, what do you need to know to understand what all these scripts are doing:

* Level Construction

Unlike most other Scratch Projects where levels are broken in to large hand drawn sprite costumes, Scratchnapped's levels are tile based (Designed as a grid of 32x32 pixel tiles, typically around 120 tiles wide and 40 tiles high...  level vary).  A tile could be a grass tile, a brick tile, a cloud tile, an enemy tile (blob, hedgehog, etc) or a spike tile, etc.  The good thing about this is that we are free to rearrange all the tiles to make any kind of level we like.  Not only are these tiles used to draw the games levels, but they are also used for hit-detection.  Again Scratchnapped departs from many other Scratch projects in that it does not make much use of the 'touching' blocks, but instead works out whether things are touching by looking at where they are in the level tiles and checking the tile type.  This is much faster, and allows for much more complex & interesting level interactions (wall jumping / hanging, etc).  Also, and more crucially, we can detect whether an enemy is sitting on a platform even when he is on the other side of the level quite far off-screen.

Each tile is of a predefined type (most map directly to a specific costume of a game block, or an enemy).  These tiles are held at runtime in the list '_Level'.  However they are placed there by using custom blocks on the 'LevelLister' sprite.  For example using the custom block named 'Block' and passing it b11, 1, 2, 3, & 4 would place the Blocks sprite with a costume of 'b11' 1 block across by 2 blocks up and would repeat the block 3 blocks wide and 4 blocks down...   This was originally how I built up levels, but the scripts quickly got too long to cope with so I created a simple scripting language which you can edit in a text editor and import in to the List defined on the 'LevelLister' sprite called 'Encoded Level'.  Please see comments on the LevelLister sprite for details on how to do this.

* Level Scrolling technology

If we were to create the whole level from the tiles specified in '_Level' then we might quickly exceed scratch's 300 sprite limit.  So instead, as the level scrolls the level tiles to scratches right and left (just off screen) are created and deleted (Instigated in the ‘Blocks’ sprite by the custom block ‘Create Level Iterative’.
